chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Ala' from Isحاق ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Regarding a man who pays another man thirty dirhams for a garment, and another man pays twenty dirhams for a garment, and he sends the two garments, and this one did not recognize his garment nor did that one recognize his garment. He said: 'The two garments are sold, and the owner of the thirty receives three-fifths of the price, and the other receives two-fifths of the price.'
I said: 'Indeed, the owner of the twenty said to the owner of the thirty: Choose whichever you wish.' He said: 'He has treated him fairly.'

key_terms.أَنْصَفَهُ: treated him fairly / gave his due

ai.seo_question: How are mixed goods divided when purchased with unequal funds and become indistinguishable?
ai.summary: In this ruling from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of proportional division (*nisab*) for mixed assets of unequal value, ensuring equitable compensation based on initial investment. The narration further highlights the virtue of *insaf* (fairness/excellence), where the owner of the larger share granting priority to the other is deemed to have acted justly beyond the strict legal minimum. This reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on combining strict legal rights with moral generosity in commercial transactions.
